focus: The repo's unbounded git call sites and the safest default posture
noveltyJustification: Nine of ten findings are new to the packet: the hook chain to the hung spawnSync, the existing GIT_NO_FSMONITOR convention, the sibling unbounded call sites, the timeout precedents, the socket attribution, and the derived default posture were all unrecorded.
keyQuestions: Q1. What unset speckit.worktreeBase and removed the reaper's daemon handling, and does anything still create worktrees under .worktrees/ by default?
Q2. What is git 2.50.1's documented fsmonitor daemon lifecycle on macOS, and how do fsmonitor.socketDir, idle shutdown and git fsmonitor--daemon stop behave when the daemon is wedged?
Q3. Is event overload the real cause of the hang, or is there a known daemon deadlock in this git version, for example around --ipc-threads or the cookie-file handshake?
Q4. Which call sites in the repo's hooks and scripts run git without a timeout, and which of them should opt out of fsmonitor?
Q5. What is the safest default: fsmonitor on with worktrees outside the checkout, or fsmonitor off for the main checkout and on per worktree?

label: The proven hung site has no ceiling and no opt-out: generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:129-133 runs spawnSync git check-ignore with no timeout option and no -c core.fsmonitor=false, and the fallback at line 136 only handles a returned failure, so a hang is never rescued.

The pre-push hook runs ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs which imports buildManifestBytes from the manifest builder; the hook's own comment says the gate finishes in about a second, which is the assumption that failed.

The repository already has the fix convention: GIT_NO_FSMONITOR = ['-c','core.fsmonitor=false'] appears in cite-drift-scan.mjs, continuity-freshness.ts, check-source-tags-helper.mjs and run-check.cjs, plus git -c core.fsmonitor=false in hook-flags.sh and the QC playbook; adopting it at the hung site is the low-risk change.

Other unbounded fsmonitor-touching call sites: verify-router-sync.cjs:168 and regenerate-skill-derived.cjs:73 run check-ignore with no opt-out and no timeout; generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:111 (rev-parse) and check-source-tags-helper.mjs:206 (opt-out present) also lack timeouts.

The repo does use timeouts elsewhere: message-contract.mjs wraps every git call in GIT_TIMEOUT_MS and git-message-gate.mjs uses timeout: 3000 for rev-parse, so the fix is a choice between two existing conventions.

Roughly 59 files under .skilled spawn git; the highest-risk class is index-reading commands (check-ignore, status, ls-files) against the main checkout because those query the fsmonitor daemon; non-index commands (rev-parse, log, show, cat-file) never touch it.

Live attribution: the main-checkout daemon holds /Users/.../Public/.git/fsmonitor--daemon.ipc (PID 5979, started 10:45:09) while worktree daemons hold a fsmonitor--daemon.ipc under their per-worktree git dirs; the socket path is the attribution key because every daemon's argv is identical.

A fsmonitor reaper cannot use git fsmonitor--daemon stop as its escalation path because stop polls forever on exactly the wedged daemon a reaper must remove; reaping means signalling the PID directly, which contradicts the current reaper's never-signals-a-process invariant, so a fsmonitor reap belongs in a separate entry point with its own stated invariant.

Q5: the safest default is fsmonitor on with worktrees outside the checkout; it removes the trigger (the main daemon's event volume from ~2M worktree files) rather than masking it and keeps the benefit on the 570k-file main checkout, while the per-worktree opt-out requires extensions.worktreeConfig (absent today), loses the largest benefit and leaves worktree daemons free to wedge their own commands.

Durability requires two changes together: set speckit.worktreeBase explicitly and stop the write-back from persisting the default as policy, otherwise the next launch without SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE re-pins .worktrees and the relocation silently reverts; under every option the hook ceiling is required because a wedge can still occur in any worktree.

reason: Rejected as the default rather than ruled out as an option: it discards a measured benefit on a 570k-file checkout, and per-worktree config gives the same safety with a narrower blast radius.
All daemons share identical argv; the socket path is the only attribution key.
